subject.title: feat(msteams): Microsoft Teams voice (CVI) + video + chat + governance

question: Which Microsoft Teams CVI landing path and SDK/config boundary should OpenClaw accept for this product area: merge this full integration, land the smaller provider foundation first and split follow-ups, or move optional governance/CVI surfaces outside the bundled core/plugin path?
rationale: The patch is not a narrow bug fix; it adds public provider, channel, SDK, security, privacy, session, and governance surfaces, and an overlapping Teams CVI PR remains open, so automation cannot safely choose the product/API boundary.

options.title: Stage the provider foundation first
options.body: Use the smaller Teams voice/video foundation as the canonical base, then split governance, meeting-productivity, DLP, SDK, and rendering-driver additions into reviewable follow-ups.

options.title: Accept this full integration
options.body: Merge this PR only after explicit owner/security/API signoff that the broad bundled Teams CVI surface is the desired product boundary.

options.title: Move optional surfaces out
options.body: Keep the core/plugin boundary lean by routing optional governance, meeting, and CVI rendering surfaces to a separate plugin or companion-worker path.

recommendation.title: Stage the provider foundation first
recommendation.body: Use the smaller Teams voice/video foundation as the canonical base, then split governance, meeting-productivity, DLP, SDK, and rendering-driver additions into reviewable follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history on both the voice-call provider boundary and the msteams plugin ownership move, which are the central product-boundary questions here.
